newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY LEAGUE - Halfback Goulding predicts Lions win.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY LEAGUE - Halfback Goulding predicts Lions win.

text.p: PALMERSTON NORTH, Oct 25 - Great Britain's magical little halfback Bobbie Goulding believes the Lions are the better team and will prove it on Friday night in the second test against New Zealand at the Manawatu Showgrounds, NZPA reports.
After his brilliant efforts in the first test, Goulding was visibly gutted when New Zealand came from behind to win 17-12 at Ericsson Stadium.
"I was just so disappointed, it was really tough to take that because we'd been in a tough battle and we had the game won for 73-minutes," Goulding said.
"Then the referee (Bill Harrigan) made a decision that we thought was harsh (replacement forward Adrian Morley was sinbinned for the final 10 minutes for holding down) and it rocked us.
"But for most of the match we know we were the better side and we aim to prove that here in the second test."

He said although the team had put up with adversity in the last week with the loss in the first test, then the loss to the New Zealand Maori, and finally having the squad split up with a third of the players going home, Great Britain would show its bulldog spirit on Friday night.
"I don't think we're gone, I think we've got a great chance of winning here, we know we can play even better than we did last week," Goulding said.

"We'll come out fighting, our spirit is good and we've been preparing well. The players being sent home is really disappointing, but we're here to play a test series and we've still got our minds on the job."

The little man, who was inspirational in getting his team going forward with superb control in the first test, said having played the Kiwis, the Lions were now more aware of the strengths and weaknesses in the home team.
"Because we've played them we know what to expect this time and we know what to do against certain players," he said.
But Goulding is likely to be a marked man on Friday night with Kiwis coach Frank Endacott spending the week working on how to nullify his presence and kicking game behind the British line.
"He did do a lot of damage in the first test and we've done a lot of work on trying to stop him here," Endacott said.
"I think he is a fine player, he is just one of the best players in the game.
"If you have a look at the British side it is easy to see that all the direction comes from Goulding, as well as their kicking game. He is a vital player to their cause."
He said the Kiwis camp had done some brainstorming on how to stop Britain's linchpin.
"We've done a lot of work on him this week, and from our drills yesterday it would have showed we will be trying to put pressure on him.
"But there is one thing saying it and another thing doing it. We just have to do it otherwise it could be a tough night."
Endacott also promised that the Kiwis would start better than they did last week when for much of the game they appeared tentative and lacked the necessary self belief.
"We do have to start stronger, but in saying that we have to appreciate that the British played very well," he said.
"Don't take anything away from them, they're a good side and they showed real British spirit in that first test.
"If we can win this test by one-point we'll be doing hand-stands at the end of it," he said.
Australian Graham Annesley will control Friday night's game which kicks off at 7.30 p.m.
Teams --

Great Britain: Stuart Spruce, Alan Hunte, Kris Radlinski, Daryl Powell, Anthony Sullivan, Iestyn Harris, Bobbie Goulding; Andy Farrell, Paul Sculthorpe, Denis Betts, Terry O'Connor, Keiron Cunningham, Paul Broadbent. Reserves - Barrie-Jon Mather, Karle Hammond, Steve Molloy, Chris Joynt.

New Zealand (Squad): Matthew Ridge, Sean Hoppe, Ruben Wiki, John Timu, Richard Barnett, Gene Ngamu, Stacey Jones; Tyran Smith, Stephen Kearney, Tony Iro, Grant Young, Syd Eru, Quentin Pongia; Marc Ellis, Joe Vagana, Richard Blackmore, Logan Swann.
